input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 is a three-year, USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — the playbook's walk-away case. It fails the fallback on every material term: it spans three years rather than the current 12-month term, gives no 30-day reduction right, and imposes take-or-pay exposure rather than a true-up. It also contradicts Section 12.3 ("Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment") and sits uneasily with Section 7.1, which limits Customer to the Fees stated in each Order Form. We therefore go to the preferred position with a single in-place replacement of the commitment sentence; no other provision cross-refers to Section 2.1, so no collateral edits are needed.

ops.oldText: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment and will pay only for Services used or ordered during the applicable term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the three-year, USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment, which our playbook treats as walk-away territory because it carries no reduction or termination right, and replaced it with payment for Services used or ordered. If a commitment is commercially essential, we can discuss a fallback limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up rather than a penalty.
proposal.summary: Replace the multi-year take-or-pay minimum with usage/ordered-Services payment only.

mappings.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
